en: The Buddha-spoken *Anuttara-sthāna Sūtra*, translator unknown;
now appended to the Catalogue of the Eastern Jin.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
“There are three unsurpassed states; listen attentively, and I shall speak of them for you.
The bhikṣus replied to the Buddha:
“Very well, we shall receive your instruction.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:
“There are three unsurpassed states:”
First, the unsurpassed state of the Buddha;
second, the unsurpassed state of the Dharma;
third, the unsurpassed state of the Saṅgha.

Whether among those sentient beings who have two feet, four feet, no feet, or many feet; whether they are with form or formless, percipient or non-percipient, or neither percipient nor non-percipient—the Tathāgata declares himself to be the unsurpassed one among them.

“Monks! If there are sentient beings who can give rise to a mind of faith and inclination toward the unsurpassed state of the Buddha, they shall obtain the unsurpassed fruit and retribution among devas and humans.”
"Monks! This is called the first unsurpassed state. Furthermore, monks!"
Among conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, as well as among material and immaterial dharmas, the dharma of detachment from desire is the unsurpassed state. Monks!
If there are sentient beings who can give rise to a mind of faith and inclination toward this unsurpassed state, they will obtain the unsurpassed fruit of retribution among gods and humans.
"Monks! This is called the second unsurpassed state. Furthermore, monks!"
Regarding the unsurpassed state of the Saṅgha: whether among a monastic community, a group, a gathering, or a retinue, the Saṅgha of the Tathāgata’s disciples is the unsurpassed state.
"O bhikṣus!
If there are sentient beings who can give rise to a mind of faith and devotion toward this unsurpassed Saṃgha, they shall obtain the unsurpassed fruit of retribution among devas and humans."
"These are called the three unsurpassed states.
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Unsurpassed States Spoken by the Buddha.
